language_wrapper: Consider a fixed regular {n_sides}-gon. A rectangle is called admissible if each of its four sides lies entirely on either a side or a diagonal of the polygon. Among all admissible rectangles, determine how many have at least {min_side_count} of their sides lying on sides (edges) of the polygon.
hardness_rationale: The family generalizes the dodecagon to any 4m-gon and imposes an added constraint requiring at least 1 or 2 sides of the rectangle to lie on polygon sides. Counting requires pairing perpendicular normal-angle classes, building signed distance spectra by parity, aggregating unordered line-pairs by their maximum offset, and enforcing the circle-feasibility inequality b_max^2 + d_max^2 <= 1. The side-count constraint further necessitates inclusion-exclusion across pair categories (0, 1, or 2 side-lines), making the combinatorics and casework more involved than the seed.
notes: Implementation uses the unit circle model. For each normal-angle class (indexed by parity), chords produce parallel lines at signed distances cos(pi*t/n). Rectangles formed by two pairs of perpendicular chords exist exactly when the extreme vertex (b_max, d_max) lies within the unit disk, equivalently b_max^2 + d_max^2 <= 1. Parity determines which distances occur (odd: t odd includes sides; even: t even includes a diameter). Side-line tracking leverages the unique level t=1 in odd parity.
source_question: Find the number of rectangles that can be formed inside a fixed regular dodecagon ( $12$ -gon) where each side of the rectangle lies on either a side or a diagonal of the dodecagon. The diagram below shows three of those rectangles. [asy] unitsize(0.6 inch); for(int i=0; i<360; i+=30) { dot(dir(i), 4+black); draw(dir(i)--dir(i+30)); } draw(dir(120)--dir(330)); filldraw(dir(210)--dir(240)--dir(30)--dir(60)--cycle, mediumgray, linewidth(1.5)); draw((0,0.366)--(0.366,0), linewidth(1.5)); [/asy]
